mainTopic: The owner of a killing ox, an animal at הר סיני, dangerous wild animals, and a tribe led into idol worship.
overview: The amud opens by asking whether the word יוּמָת in the פסוק of a שור that killed means its owner is really put to death. The גמרא tries several answers: an argument from an extra word, a suggestion about חנק, and a proof from כופר, which is then turned around with אדרבה. It finally settles the matter with חזקיה's verse "רֹצֵחַ הוּא": a person is executed only for his own murder, never for his ox's. Next, the גמרא asks how many judges an animal at הר סיני needed, and it learns from the פסוק that, like a man, it needed twenty-three. Then ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue whether a lion or wolf may be killed only after it has killed. A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש, showing that 'זכה' means a merit in Heaven. The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא differs from the תנא קמא about a snake. Finally, it asks what kind of tribe is judged by seventy-one, answers that it is a tribe led into idol worship, and finds that this seems to fit neither רבי יאשיה nor רבי יונתן. רב מתנה begins his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the owner really gets the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier reading of יוּמָת. Maybe the word is teaching that the ox's owner is actually put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say that this word comes to teach that the owner is put to death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier reading of "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת". Maybe it simply means the owner is executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, יוּמָת was read as a comparison: the ox is judged like its owner would be. The challenge offers the plain meaning instead, that the owner himself is liable to death. If that is right, the earlier comparison falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (the opening of a challenge)

phrases.english: Say that it comes to teach death!
phrases.notes: "It" is the word יוּמָת in "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת". The question is: maybe it means the owner himself gets killed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading of יוּמָת as comparing the ox's judgment to the owner's.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that יוּמָת only compares the ox's death to the owner's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of יוּמָת is that the owner is executed, so it may not be a comparison at all.

steps.title: Then the Torah should have stopped at "and also its owner"
steps.stepSummary: If the owner were really to be killed, "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו" would be enough. The extra word יוּמָת must be there to teach the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the Torah write "and also its owner" and stop there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that if the owner were meant to die, the Torah could have written only "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The ox shall be stoned, and also its owner" would already tell us the owner dies. Since the Torah added יוּמָת anyway, that word must teach something else. It teaches that the ox's death is judged like the owner's death.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it be silent, stop there

phrases.english: If so, let it write
"And also its owner," and be silent!
phrases.notes: Without the word יוּמָת, the פסוק would read "the ox shall be stoned, and also its owner."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra-word argument: the added word must teach something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יוּמָת might mean the owner is executed.
steps.terutzMaskana: If execution were meant, "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו" alone would suffice, so יוּמָת teaches the comparison.

steps.title: Without יוּמָת we would think the owner is stoned
steps.stepSummary: The answer is pushed back. The word יוּמָת is not extra, because without it we would think the owner is stoned like his ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written it that way, I would have said the owner is executed by stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 2 by showing that the word יוּמָת is not extra after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only "וְגַם בְּעָלָיו", the owner would be tied to the ox's punishment of stoning. The word יוּמָת is then needed to show he gets a different death. That means יוּמָת could still be about a real death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written it this way,
I would have said by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא הָכִי, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the extra-word argument of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that יוּמָת is extra.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Without יוּמָת we would think the owner is stoned, so the word has a job even if he really dies.

steps.title: Stoning for the owner makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The pushback is rejected. Nobody would think the owner gets stoning, since a man who kills with his own hands only gets the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you really think by stoning? If he himself killed, he gets the sword, and if his property killed, he would get stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 3 that we would ever think the owner is stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real murderer is killed with סייף, which is lighter than סקילה. The owner's animal killing someone cannot make him worse off than killing with his own hands. So we would never think stoning, the word יוּמָת is extra again, and the answer of step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The sword, the death penalty for a murderer

phrases.english: By stoning, would that enter your mind?
If he himself killed, it is by the sword,
and if his property killed, by stoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 and so brings back the answer of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that we would think the owner is stoned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An owner cannot be punished more harshly for his ox's act than a murderer is for his own act.

steps.title: Maybe יוּמָת gives the owner a lighter death
steps.stepSummary: A new suggestion: maybe יוּמָת means the owner is executed, but with the lighter death of חנק instead of סייף. This works only for the view that חנק is lighter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the Torah wrote "shall be put to death" to be lenient with him, moving him from the sword to strangulation? That is fine for the one who says strangulation is harsher, but for the one who says strangulation is lighter, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new way the word יוּמָת could still mean a real death penalty: a lighter one, חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah, a plain "יוּמָת" usually means חנק. So maybe the owner dies, but more gently than a murderer. For the view that חנק is harsher than סייף this cannot be, since the owner cannot be worse off than a murderer. For the view that חנק is lighter, the suggestion works, and the גמרא needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Strangulation, one of the four court deaths
This works well according to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. Only for the one who says חנק is lighter does this question work. For the one who says חנק is harsher, it was never a question.

phrases.english: But perhaps this that the Merciful One wrote, "shall be put to death"
is to be lenient with him,
to take him out of the sword and into strangulation?
This works well for the one who says strangulation is harsher,
but for the one who says strangulation is lighter,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא הַאי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״יוּמָת״ לְאַקּוֹלֵי עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that stoning is ruled out, but offers another reason יוּמָת is needed while still meaning a real death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion of step 2 that יוּמָת is extra and only teaches the comparison.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוּמָת could be needed to give the owner חנק instead of סייף, at least for the view that חנק is lighter.

steps.title: The ransom proves the owner is not liable to death
steps.stepSummary: The Torah lets the owner pay a כופר, and the Torah forbids taking a כופר from a murderer. So the owner is not truly liable to death, and יוּמָת must teach the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would not enter your mind, because it is written: "If a ransom is placed upon him." And if you think he is liable to death, isn't it written: "You shall not take a ransom for the life of a murderer"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the חנק idea with a proof from two פסוקים about כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of the ox lets the owner pay ransom money. Yet the Torah says that someone truly liable to death can never pay a ransom. Since the owner can pay, he seems not to be liable to death at all. The next step turns this proof around, so it does not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom money paid instead of a punishment

phrases.english: It would not enter your mind,
for it is written: "If a ransom is placed upon him."

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא,
phrases.english: And if you think he is liable to death,
isn't it written: "You shall not take a ransom for the life of a murderer"!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״אִם כֹּפֶר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a proof from כופר that the owner is not liable to death. Step 7 then rejects this proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from other פסוקים that rules out any real death penalty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יוּמָת might give the owner a real but lighter death, חנק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner can pay כופר, and a person liable to death cannot, so he is not liable to death at all.

steps.title: The ransom payment actually shows the owner deserves death
steps.stepSummary: The proof from כופר is turned around. The כופר shows the owner deserves death but is allowed to pay money instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, that very point works the other way. If he killed with his own hands, money is not enough, and only death will do. If his ox killed, let him save his life with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 6. The כופר does not prove the owner is free from death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said: you can never take a כופר from a murderer, so an owner who pays one must not truly deserve death. Now the גמרא says the opposite: maybe he does deserve death, and the Torah just lets him buy his way out because only his ox killed. That would explain why the word יוּמָת is needed, so the proof for the comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the argument works the other way

steps.confusionAlert: The same fact, that the owner can pay a כופר, is used for both sides. In step 6 it proved he does not deserve death. Here it is read as: he deserves death, but money can replace it.

phrases.english: On the contrary, because of that very point:
If he himself killed,
money is not enough for him,
only death.
If his ox killed,
let him redeem his life with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from כופר that the owner is not truly liable to death
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כופר can be read as a way out of a real death sentence, not as proof that there is no death sentence

steps.title: חזקיה's verse: you are killed only for your own murder
steps.stepSummary: Since the earlier verses do not settle it, the גמרא brings a different פסוק from חזקיה that clearly frees the owner from death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, חזקיה said, and so the school of חזקיה taught: The verse says, 'The one who struck shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer.' For his own murder you kill him, but you do not kill him for his ox's murder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier proofs and brings a new, clear source. The owner of an ox that killed is not executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he is a murderer' limit the death penalty to the person who did the killing himself. An ox's killing is not counted as the owner's murder. This settles that the owner is not put to death, so the word יוּמָת in the ox section must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; dropping the earlier approach for a new one

steps.whatToRemember: A person is executed only for a murder he did himself (רציחתו), never for a death caused by his ox.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final source that the owner of a killing ox is free from human punishment by death.

phrases.english: Rather, Chizkiyah said,
and so the school of Chizkiyah taught:
The verse says,
"The one who struck shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer" –
for his own murder you kill him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה הוֹרְגוֹ עַל רְצִיחַת שׁוֹרוֹ.
phrases.english: but you do not kill him for his ox's murder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כופר proof is rejected, brings a new verse to settle the question
steps.raayaObject: The owner of an ox that killed is not executed

steps.title: How many judges for an animal at הר סיני?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: an animal that touched הר סיני had to be killed. Did it need a court of twenty-three like other animals sentenced to death?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: An ox at סיני, by how many judges? Do we learn a one-time rule from the rule for all generations, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It is setting up a search for an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an animal sentenced to death is judged by twenty-three. The rule at הר סיני was only for that moment (שעה). The question is whether a one-time law follows the permanent rules (דורות) or not.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a question was raised
An ox that touched הר סיני at מתן תורה
A one-time rule, only for that moment
Rules that apply for all generations
Do we learn (one from the other)?

phrases.english: They asked:
An ox at Sinai, by how many judges?
phrases.notes: At מתן תורה any animal that touched the mountain was to be killed.

phrases.english: Do we learn a one-time rule from a rule for all generations,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about animals judged for death
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the one-time case of an animal at הר סיני needed a court of twenty-three

steps.title: Animal at הר סיני is judged by twenty-three, like a man
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching compares the animal to the man in the same פסוק, so both need twenty-three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear what רמי בר יחזקאל taught: 'Whether animal or man, it shall not live.' Just as a man is judged by twenty-three, so too an animal is judged by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The animal at הר סיני needed twenty-three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק at הר סיני puts animal and man side by side. A man who is sentenced to death always needs a court of twenty-three. So the animal in the same verse also needs twenty-three.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-three, the court size for death cases

steps.whatToRemember: Even the one-time animal at הר סיני was judged by twenty-three, because the פסוק compares it to a man.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל:
phrases.english: Come hear, for Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
"Whether animal or man, it shall not live" –
just as a man is judged by twenty-three,
so too an animal is judged by twenty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Twenty-three judges, learned from the comparison of animal and man in the same פסוק

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only a lion or wolf that killed
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה about a lion or wolf, ריש לקיש says the case is only one that killed. He seems to hold that these animals can be tamed and can have owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lion and the wolf, etc. ריש לקיש said: This is only when they killed, but if they did not kill, no. So he must hold that they can be tamed and they can have owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about a lion or wolf. ריש לקיש limits it to an animal that already killed someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wild animal can be tamed, it might belong to someone. So you may not just kill it unless it killed a person. That is why ריש לקיש limits the משנה to an animal that killed.

phrases.english: The lion and the wolf, etc.
Reish Lakish said:
And this is when they killed,
but if they did not kill – no.
Apparently he holds:
they can be tamed
and they can have owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאֲרִי וְהַזְּאֵב כּוּ׳. אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next case of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה speaks only of a lion or wolf that killed; one that did not kill may not be killed, since it can be tamed and owned

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even if they did not kill
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה applies even to a lion or wolf that did not kill. He seems to hold they cannot be tamed and have no owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even if they did not kill. So he must hold that they cannot be tamed and they have no owners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with ריש לקיש. He says the משנה includes even wild animals that have not killed anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If these animals can never be tamed, they never belong to anyone. Killing one hurts no owner, so it may be killed even before it does harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though they did not kill

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even though they did not kill.
Apparently he holds:
they cannot be tamed
and they have no owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵמִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with ריש לקיש in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lion or wolf may be killed even if it did not kill, since it cannot be tamed and has no owner

steps.title: What does the first killer gain according to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says whoever kills these animals first gains. That fits רבי יוחנן, since he gets the hide. But for ריש לקיש the animal already killed, so it is forbidden for any benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי אליעזר says, whoever kills them first gains. This works for רבי יוחנן: what does he gain? He gains their hides. But according to ריש לקיש, what does he gain? Since they killed, the רבנן treated them like animals whose sentence was already given, and they are forbidden for any benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the words of רבי אליעזר in the משנה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן the animal has no owner and no ban on it, so the first killer keeps the hide. For ריש לקיש the animal already killed a person. So it is treated as if it was already sentenced, and an animal like that is forbidden for any benefit. Then the word 'gains' seems to mean nothing for him.

keyTerms.meaning: It works fine for (one view, but not for the other)

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Whoever kills them first gains.
This works fine for Rabbi Yochanan:
What does he gain? He gains their hides.
But according to Reish Lakish,
what does he gain?
Since they killed,
the Rabbis treated them like ones whose sentence was already given,
and they are forbidden for any benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַקּוֹדֵם לְהוֹרְגָן זָכָה. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two views of steps 11 and 12 against the משנה, and challenges ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the משנה speaks only of animals that killed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal that killed is treated as already sentenced and is forbidden for benefit, so the first killer would gain nothing, yet רבי אליעזר says he gains

steps.title: 'Merits' means a merit in Heaven
steps.stepSummary: For ריש לקיש, 'זכה' in רבי אליעזר's words means he earns a מצוה, not that he gets to keep the animal's hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he merits' mean? He merits in the eyes of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13 on ריש לקיש. It says 'זכה' does not mean he gains something he can own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that an animal that killed is forbidden for any benefit, so nobody can 'gain' its hide. The answer changes the meaning of 'זכה': the person who kills the dangerous animal gains a מצוה, because he removed a danger. No money or hide is involved at all.

keyTerms.meaning: In the eyes of Heaven, a spiritual merit

phrases.english: What is 'he merits'?
He merits in the eyes of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זכה' means he gains the animal's hide, which can only fit an animal that did not kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זכה' means he gains a מצוה, which fits even an animal that already killed.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the whole argument is about animals that killed, and רבי אליעזר there says 'זכה בהן לשמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that fits ריש לקיש: An ox that killed, and any other tame or wild animal that killed, are judged by twenty-three. רבי אליעזר says: An ox that killed is judged by twenty-three, but other tame and wild animals that killed, whoever kills them first merits with them in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up ריש לקיש on both points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the ברייתא talks only about animals 'שהמיתו', that killed, just as ריש לקיש said. Second, רבי אליעזר's words openly say 'לשמים', which matches the answer in Step 14 that 'זכה' is a spiritual merit.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports him

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute about lions, wolves and the like is about animals that already killed, and 'זכה' means a merit in Heaven. This supports ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with ריש לקיש:
Both an ox that killed
and a tame or wild animal that killed –
are judged by twenty-three.
רבי אליעזר says:
An ox that killed – by twenty-three,
but other tame and wild animals that killed –
whoever kills them first
merits through them in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 14 and ריש לקיש's position from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that the case is an animal that killed, and that 'זכה' means a merit in Heaven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא) that says 'שהמיתו' and 'זכה בהן לשמים'.

steps.title: Is רבי עקיבא saying the same as the first תנא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says these animals are judged by twenty-three, which sounds like the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי עקיבא says, etc. Isn't רבי עקיבא the same as the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and asks what רבי עקיבא adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said these dangerous animals need twenty-three judges. רבי עקיבא also says twenty-three. So the גמרא asks what the difference between them is.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says, etc.
Isn't רבי עקיבא the same as the first תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא.

steps.title: The difference is a snake
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions argue about a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא disagree about a snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא includes a snake in the list that needs twenty-three judges. רבי עקיבא includes the other animals but not a snake, so a snake does not need a court.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: The difference between them is a snake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about a snake: the תנא קמא requires twenty-three for it, רבי עקיבא does not.

steps.title: What sin did the tribe commit?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a tribe is judged only by seventy-one. The גמרא asks what sin it did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: We do not judge, etc. This tribe that sinned, with what did it sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, about judging a whole שבט, and asks which sin is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a tribe can only be judged by the big סנהדרין of seventy-one. But it does not say what the tribe did. The גמרא wants to know the exact case.

phrases.english: We do not judge, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: we judge a tribe only in a court of seventy-one.

phrases.english: This tribe that sinned, with what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sin the 'tribe that sinned' in the משנה committed.

steps.title: It can't be a tribe that broke שבת
steps.stepSummary: The תורה treats a group differently from individuals only for עבודת כוכבים, not for other מצוות like שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a tribe that broke שבת: we can say the Torah makes a difference between individuals and a large group for עבודת כוכבים, but for other מצוות does it make a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer, that the tribe broke שבת, and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only for עבודת כוכבים does the תורה have a special law for a group (עיר הנדחת). For other sins like שבת, a whole tribe is just many individual sinners, so there would be no reason for a special court of seventy-one.

phrases.english: If you say a tribe that broke שבת,
we can say the Merciful One distinguishes
between individuals and a large group
regarding idol worship,
but for other מצוות, does He distinguish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible answer to Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה's tribe broke שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה gives group-sinners a special law only for עבודת כוכבים, so a tribe that broke שבת would need no special court.

steps.title: A tribe that was led into idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a tribe that was pushed into עבודת כוכבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a tribe that was led astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the tribe in the משנה served עבודת כוכבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only עבודת כוכבים has a special group law, the sinning tribe must be one that was talked into idol worship. This makes the special court of seventy-one make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: That was led astray into idol worship

phrases.english: Rather, it is a tribe that was led astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to Step 18 after rejecting the שבת idea in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tribe in the משנה was led into עבודת כוכבים.

steps.title: Whose view is this? Not רבי יאשיה and not רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: If a whole tribe is judged like a group, the משנה seems to fit neither רבי יאשיה nor רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean we judge it with the law of a large group? Then whose view is it? Not רבי יאשיה and not רבי יונתן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 20. If a whole tribe gets the group law of עיר הנדחת, no known תנא seems to say so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling this a tribe that served idols means it gets the group law, like an עיר הנדחת. But both רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן set an upper limit on how many people can make an עיר הנדחת, and a whole tribe goes past both limits. The source for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of a large group

phrases.english: Is this to say that with the law of a large group
we judge it?
Like whom?

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן!
phrases.english: Not like רבי יאשיה and not like רבי יונתן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's tribe served idols and is judged with the group law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known opinions limit עיר הנדחת to a size smaller than a whole tribe, so no one would judge a whole tribe with the group law.

steps.title: The ברייתא on the size of an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה says ten to one hundred; רבי יונתן says one hundred up to most of a tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: How big can an עיר הנדחת be? From ten to one hundred, says רבי יאשיה. רבי יונתן says: From one hundred until most of a tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves its challenge from Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה's top limit is one hundred people. רבי יונתן's top limit is most of a tribe, not a whole one. So a full tribe is bigger than both limits, and neither would give it the law of an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: A city that was led into idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: Both numbers are limits. Going above the top number means it is no longer an עיר הנדחת, so a whole tribe is too big for both views.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
Up to how many do we make an עיר הנדחת?
phrases.notes: He means how many people in the city must serve idols for it to get this law.

phrases.english: From ten until one hundred,
these are the words of רבי יאשיה.
רבי יונתן says:
From one hundred until most of a tribe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: עַד כַּמָּה עוֹשִׂין עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the challenge in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that neither רבי יאשיה nor רבי יונתן would judge a whole tribe with the law of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the size limits of an עיר הנדחת according to רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן.

steps.title: Even the larger opinion stops at most of a tribe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its difficulty: רבי יונתן allows up to most of a tribe, but not an entire tribe, so a whole tribe cannot be treated as an עיר הנדחת according to anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יונתן only said 'most of it,' but the whole tribe, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it began in step 21. It shows that neither רבי יאשיה nor even רבי יונתן allows the group law for an entire tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה's limit (10 to 100) is too small for a tribe. רבי יונתן's limit is bigger, but it stops at most of a tribe. So a case where the whole tribe served עבודת כוכבים is outside both opinions, and the משנה's case looks like it fits no one.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of it (most of the tribe)
A city led into עבודת כוכבים, judged as a group

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יונתן allows any size at all. His opinion has an upper limit too: most of a tribe, not a whole tribe.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא רוּבּוֹ,
phrases.english: And even Rabbi Yonatan only said a majority of it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the tribe, going back to רבי יונתן's range in step 22.

phrases.english: but all of it, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי יונתן's range quoted in step 22 to complete the difficulty from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 20 that the משנה's tribe was led into עבודת כוכבים and is judged as a group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A whole tribe is bigger than the maximum size (most of a tribe) allowed even by רבי יונתן, so the group law cannot apply to it.

steps.title: רב מתנה begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה starts to answer the difficulty by saying 'here,' pointing to how the משנה's case should be understood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: Here...
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens רב מתנה's answer. The גמרא is setting up the next move, and the rest of his explanation comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'here' tells us רב מתנה is about to explain what case the משנה is really talking about. So far, he gives only the opening word; the actual answer to the difficulty follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (in this case, in our משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said: Here,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to the difficulty completed in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה (only the opening word appears so far)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to describe a whole tribe judged under the group law, which fits no opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated here; רב מתנה's explanation of the case continues next.
